Richard Roe, a resident of Jacksonville, in Duval County, Florida, brings this bill of complaint against John Doe and Mary Doe, his wife, both of whom are residents of Jacksonville, in Duval County, Florida, and alleges: 

1. The defendant, John Doe, on the 1st day of January, 1930, being indebted to the plaintiff in the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,- 000.00), as evidence of such indebtedness, on that day executed and delivered to the plaintiff his promissory note in the principal sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00), said note being payable one year after date with interest thereon at the rate of 6% per annum from its date until paid. Said note was not paid at the maturity date thereof and, on the 10th day of August, 1931, the plaintiff filed an action at law in this court to recover judgment against the defendant John Doe on said note. Said defendant was duly served with process in said suit, but he failed to enter his appearance therein and a default was entered against him on the rule day in October, 1931. Thereafter, on the 31st day of December, 1931, a final judgment was entered against the defendant John Doe in said action at law for the sum of five thousand six hundred dollars ($5,600.00), together with interest and costs. 

Said final judgment is recorded 'n Minute Book 75, page 150, of the records of this court. A certified copy of said final judgment is hereto attached, marked Exhibit "A," and made a part of this bill of complaint. Said judgment is now outstanding and unpaid and has not been set aside, superseded, or amended. 

2. On the 1st day of January, 1930, and at all times thereafter until the 1st day of October, 1931, the defendant John Doe was the owner in fee simple of a tract of land situated and being in Duval County,

FORMS 

883 Florida, more particularly described as the northeast quarter (NE¼4) of section two (2), in township three (3) south, of range twenty-seven (27) east. 3. On the 1st day of October, 1931, the defendant John Doe, by a warranty deed executed and delivered on that day, conveyed to the defendant Mary Doe, his wife, the said land described in paragraph 2 of this bill of complaint. Said deed was thereupon, on the 1st day of

Said conveyance was in fact gratuitous and voluntary, and was made, executed, and contrived of fraud, covin, collusion, and guile and with the purpose and intent to delay, hinder, embarrass, and defraud the plaintiff of his just and lawful claim against the defendant John Doe. Form No. 8 BILL FOR TEMPORARY AND PERMANENT INJUNCTION AGAINST PRIVATE NUISANCE 

VS. 

William Smith,

Defendant Bill of Complaint 

John Doe, a resident of Clearwater, in Pinellas County, Florida, brings this bill of complaint against William Smith, a resident of Clearwater, in Pinellas County, Florida, and alleges: 

1. In the month of February, 1932, plaintiff purchased the property known as Lot fourteen (14) of the Gulf View subdivision, in the city of Clearwater, Pinellas County, Florida, a plat of said subdivision being recorded in Plat Book A, page 15, of the public records of said county. 

Said lots were conveyed to the plaintiff by a deed executed on February 10, 1932, and recorded on that day in Deed Book 160, page 425, of the public records of Pinellas County, Florida. In 1934, the plaintiff erected a dwelling house upon said property at a cost of approximately fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00). Since the construction of said dwelling house in 1934, plaintiff has occupied it as a home and place of residence annually between the months of November and 

April, inclusive. 

2. The Gulf View subdivision is one of the highest class residential sections of the city of Clearwater, and except for the property of the defendant hereinafter described, it contains no buildings except private, single family residences. Other than the building of the defendant hereinafter described, there is no building used for business purposes within a radius of approximately one quarter of a mile from the property of the plaintiff. 

3. In the year 1936, the defendant, William Smith, purchased the property known as Lot twenty (20) of the Gulf View subdivision in the city of Clearwater, Pinellas County, Florida. This property is directly in the rear of the aforesaid property of the plaintiff and the western boundary of the defendant's property adjoins and is co-ex-

tensive with the eastern boundary of the plaintiff's property, all of which is more particularly shown by a map hereto attached, marked Exhibit "A," and made a part of this bill of complaint. 

4. In the year 1936, the defendant, William Smith, erected a building on his said property in the nature of a club house and bar, with rooms for reading, card playing, and other forms of entertainment. 

In the rear of this club house the defendant then constructed an open air garden restaurant, including a dance platform and music stand. 

Said restaurant is known as the Patio Patricia and has been advertised as a place for dancing as well as for luncheons and dinners. The orchestra stand in said restaurant is at a distance of one hundred and fifty feet from the rear of plaintiff's home and the bedroom occupied by him in said home. The dance platform in said restaurant is at a distance of not more than one hundred twenty feet from the rear of plaintiff's home and from his said bedroom. Two windows in the plaintiff's bedroom face the defendant's restaurant and overlook it. 

All of this more fully appears from the map hereto attached as Exhibit "A." 

5. Said restaurant, known as the Patio Patricia, opened for business on December 15, 1936. On said day, numerous musicians employed by the defendant played dance music and sang from early in the evening until after midnight. As the evening progressed, the noise from the orchestra grew louder and louder, and at times the dancers, as well as the members of the orchestra, sang, shouted, and yelled. 

During the evening, many patrons of said restaurant purchased intoxicating beverages, became intoxicated, and created much noise and confusion by loud talking, singing, and shouting. 

6. On the said night of December 15, 1936, plaintiff was kept awake and deprived of sleep until long after midnight and was harassed, worried, and annoyed by the aforesaid noises coming from the defendant's restaurant. These noises could be plainly heard in the defendant's bedroom and were of sufficient volume to prevent a person of normal sensibilities from sleeping. The said noises could also be plainly heard in all parts of the plaintiff's home, and the constant and continual repetition of said noises was a serious discomfort, distress, and inconvenience to the plaintiff and the members of his family, and would have been a source of discomfort, distress, and inconvenience to any person of normal sensibilities.

FORMS 

889 7. On each and every night since December 15, 1936, the defendant has operated his said restaurant in the manner hereinabove described, and on each and every night since December 15, 1936, the plaintiff has been kept awake and deprived of sleep, rest, repose, and tranquillity until long after midnight by the operation of said restaurant in the manner aforesaid and by the noises emanating therefrom. The constant repetition of these noises on each and every night since December 15, 1936, has caused and continues to cause the plaintiff serious annoyance and discomfort as well as mental and physical distress and suffering and irreparable injury to his health, and said noises will, if continued, cause serious and irreparable injury to the comfort and health of any person of normal sensibilities occupying the home of the plaintiff. 

8. Because the aforesaid noises from the defendant's restaurant can be so plainly heard in all parts of the plaintiff's home, and because these noises will seriously impair the comfort and health of any person of normal sensibilities occupying said home, the value of the plaintiff's property will, if these noises are continued, depreciate to the extent of fifty per cent of its actual value, and it will be impossible for the plaintiff to sell or rent his said home at its true value as long as the defendant operates his restaurant in the aforesaid manner. 

9. The action of the defendant in conducting said restaurant in the manner aforesaid is causing and, unless restrained, will continue to cause irreparable injury to the plaintiff, and the plaintiff is without any remedy at law. 

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff prays (a) that the defendant, William

Smith, his agents, servants, and employees, and each and every of them, be perpetually enjoined and restrained from playing instrumental music of any kind and from singing in the defendant's said restaurant after the hour of ten o'clock, P. M., of each night, and (b) that plaintiff be granted a preliminary injunction pending the final hearing and decision of this cause whereby the defendant, his agents, servants, and employees are enjoined and restrained as hereinabove prayed.

To secure the payment to the plaintiff, John Doe, of the said sums of money, the defendants, William Smith and Mary Smith, his wife, did, on or about February 18, 1929, and as of that date, make, execute, and deliver to the plaintiff their mortgage deed, therein and thereby reciting and setting forth the indebtedness evidenced by said promissory note above described, and did give unto the plaintiff a

893 mortgage lien upon all that lot, parcel, or piece of land lying and being in the City of Jacksonville, Duval County, Florida, then in the possession of the said mortgagors and to which they or one of them claimed the fee simple title, more particularly described as Lot six (6), Block three (3), Avondale, according to plat thereof recorded in Plat Book 17, page 12, of the current public records of Duval County, Florida, together with all and singular the tenements, hereditaments, easements, and appurtenances thereunto belonging or in anywise appertaining, and the rents, issues, income, revenue, and profits therefrom. 

3. Said mortgage was upon the condition that, if the said mortgagors should pay or cause to be paid the moneys mentioned in said promissory note, and the interest thereon, in the manner therein specified, and all other sums provided to be paid by said mortgage, and should perform all other covenants of said mortgage, then said mortgage and the estate thereby granted should cease, determine, and be absolutely null and void. 

4. Said mortgage was filed for record in the public records of 

Duval County, Florida, on March 14, 1929, and was therein recorded in Mortgage Book 454, page 252, all of which more fully appears from a copy of said mortgage hereto attached, marked Exhibit "B," and made a part of this bill of complaint.

(c) To pay all costs, charges, abstract fees, and expenses, including attorney's fees, which the said mortgagee may be put to or incur in collecting the sums secured by said mortgage. (d) To permit, commit, or suffer no waste, and to keep all improvements on said mortgaged property in good condition, and to do or permit to be done to said property nothing that may in any way impair or weaken the security under said mortgage.

6. Said mortgage note matured on February 18, 1932, and was not then paid, nor has the principal sum so due, or any part thereof, since been paid, and the same is now due and for more than one month last past has been overdue and unpaid, and no extension of time for the payment thereof has been given or granted. No interest on said mortgage note has been paid since February 18, 1930. 

7. The taxes levied and assessed by the City of Jacksonville upon said mortgaged property and premises for the year 1930 in the sum of $30.52 are now unpaid and delinquent and penalties and interest have accrued thereon, in breach of the covenants of the mortgage herein sought to be foreclosed and by reason thereof the plaintiff hereby exercises the privilege vested in him by the terms of said mortgage and declares all sums and amounts thereby secured to be immediately due and payable. BILL AGAINST CO-TENANT FOR PARTITION, ACCOUNTING, INJUNCTION, AND RECEIVER 

In the Circuit Court in and for St. Lucie County, Florida. In Chancery. 

VS. 

William Smith,

Defendant Bill of Complaint 

John Doe, a resident of Fort Pierce, in St. Lucie County, Florida, brings this bill of complaint against William Smith, a resident of Fort 

Pierce, in St. Lucie County, Florida, and alleges: 

1. On the first day of January, 1930, plaintiff was the owner of an undivided one-third interest in fee simple in the following described real estate lying and being in St. Lucie County, Florida, to wit, northeast quarter (NE) of the northwest quarter (NW14) of Section 32, Township 36 South, Range 38 East. Plaintiff at the present time is, and at all times since the first day of January, 1930, has been, the owner in fee simple of the said undivided one-third interest in said land.

FORMS 

905 2. On the first day of January, 1930, and at all times since that date, up to and including the present time, the remaining undivided twothirds interest in said land has been owned by the defendant William Smith. 

3. The defendant William Smith was, on the first day of January, 1930, in the sole possession of the said land, and at all times since that date, up to and including the present time, he has continued in the sole possession of the said land and has received, collected, and used the rents, issues, and profits thereof and has sold and caused to be sold certain crops of oranges from trees growing upon the said property. 

The exact value of the said rents, issues, and profits is unknown to the plaintiff. 

4. The defendant, though often requested to do so, has failed and neglected to account to the plaintiff, or to pay over to the plaintiff, the share of the plaintiff in the rents, issues, and profits of the said land, and the defendant has utterly failed to account to the plaintiff for the defendant's use of the said property as aforesaid. 

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff prays (a) that an accounting be taken under the order of this court of the rents, issues, and profits of the said real estate since the first day of January, 1930, and that the defendant be required to pay over to the plaintiff one-third of the value of such rents, issues, and profits, (b) that a partition of the above described property be decreed by this court in accordance with law, and that one-third of the said property, or one-third of the proceeds of the sale thereof, be conveyed to the plaintiff, (c) that the defendant be enjoined from converting any crops or the proceeds of any crops hereafter maturing upon the property to his own use and from paying over any share of the plaintiff in said proceeds to any person other than the plaintiff, and that a temporary injunction be issued as above prayed, and (d) that a receiver be appointed with the usual powers of a receiver in chancery to take possession of the said property and to administer it under the orders of this court for the benefit of the owners thereof, and to pay into this court all the rents, issues, and profits of the said property to be disposed of as equity may require. 

Solicitor for Plaintiff Note.

The foregoing form is based upon a bill of complaint set out and held sufficient in Carlton v. Hilliard, 64 Fla. 228, 60 So. 220. A bill including a cause of action for partition must be sworn to. See Chapter XXIX, Section

318, supra.

Likewise, a bill containing a prayer for a temporary injunction or for a receiver must be verified. See Chapter XXVI, Section 270, supra, Chapter XXXI, Section 345, supra. See Form No. 7, Appendix B, for form of affidavit.

A form of decree of partition and appointing commissioners to make the same, and a form of final decree on the commissioner's report, are set out in 

Williams v. Clyatt, 53 Fla. 987, 43 So. 441.

Form No. 15 BILL TO QUIET TITLE UNDER THE 1925 STATUTE (C. G. L. 5010 ET SEQ.) 

VS. 

William Smith, et al., Defendants

Bill of Complaint 

John Doe, a resident of Pinellas County, Florida, brings this bill of complaint against William Smith, if living, and, if dead, against his unknown heirs, devisees, legatees, or grantees, and against any and all persons having or claiming any right, title, or interest in and to the lands hereinafter described, and alleges: 

1. Plaintiff is the owner in fee simple and in the actual, physical, and exclusive possession of that tract or parcel of land in Pinellas County, Florida, more particularly described as the northeast quarter (NE) of the southwest quarter (SW14) of Section twelve (12), Township 18 South, Range 20 East. 

2. Plaintiff and the defendants herein named, designated, or specified, claim any and all right, title, and interest they or any of them have or are vested with or entitled to from and under a common source, to wit, a deed from David Taylor and Henrietta Taylor, his wife, to

William Smith, which deed is dated February 25, 1909, and is recorded in Deed Book 42, page 79, of the public records of Pinellas County, Florida. 

3. There is no conveyance out of the said William Smith of said land, but, on August 3, 1919, one Richard Smith executed and delivered a deed to said land to John Doe, the plaintiff herein, said deed being recorded in Deed Book 73, page 19, of the public records of Pinellas

FORMS 

907 County, Florida. It is recited in and by said deed that Richard Smith, the grantor therein, is the sole heir of the defendant William Smith, and that he executed said deed as such sole heir, all of which more fully appears from a copy of said deed hereto attached, marked Exhibit "A," and made a part of this bill of complaint. 

4. Plaintiff has been, for more than seven years last past, in the actual, continuous, open, notorious, and exclusive possession, and in the undisturbed occupation of, all and singular the property and premises above described and involved in this suit. This possession has been evidenced by cultivation, by tenants and agents of the plaintiff, of said property for the purpose of growing thereon crops of vegetables and other plants usually and ordinarily grown and harvested annually in kitchen and truck gardens, and by maintaining thereon and thereabout fences sufficiently substantial to protect such crops from the depredations of animals and completely enclosing said property against such trespassing and invasion. Said possession has further been evidenced by grazing and keeping on said land, enclosed by a fence strong enough to keep them from escaping, farm and work animals and live stock, and also by paying, for all of said period, under claim of title, and ownership, the taxes levied and assessed on said property by Pinellas County and the State of Florida. By means of said acts, plaintiff published and generally disseminated to the world at large his claim of ownership and to the exclusive possession of said property. 

5. Plaintiff does not know, and has not been able to ascertain by diligent search and inquiry, whether the defendant William Smith is dead or alive, or, if dead, whether said Richard Smith is an heir of the said William Smith, or whether the said Richard Smith is the sole heir of the defendant William Smith. By reason of the premises, a cloud, doubt, and suspicion is cast upon the title of the plaintiff in and to the property hereinabove described, which cloud, doubt, or suspicion the plaintiff is entitled to have removed and decreed to be null and void. 

6. Plaintiff does not know, and has not been able to ascertain by diligent search and inquiry, whether the defendant William Smith is now living and, if living, the residence, place of abode, or post office address of the said defendant. Plaintiff further does not know, and has not been able to ascertain by diligent search and inquiry, whether the said defendant is now dead and, if dead, the names, ages, resi-

dences, places of abode, and post office addresses of his heirs, legatees, devisees, or grantees. Plaintiff has also made diligent search and inquiry to ascertain whether or not there are any other persons claiming any right, title, or interest in and to the lands involved in this suit, and, after such diligent search and inquiry, he has been unable to ascertain the names, ages, residences, places of abode, or whereabouts of any other persons claiming any right, title, or interest in and to the lands hereinabove described. 

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff prays (a) that the plaintiff be decreed to be the owner in fee simple of the land hereinabove described and that the title of the plaintiff to said land be forever quieted and confirmed in him, and (b) that all claims, rights, titles, and interests of the defendant William Smith, and of his heirs, legatees, devisees, or grantees, and of all persons claiming by, through, or under him, or them, or any of them, since the filing of the lis pendens herein, as well as the claims of any other persons in and to said land, be forever cancelled and decreed to be null and void and held for naught. 

Solicitor for Plaintiff Note. The principal allegations of the foregoing bill of complaint are based upon quotations from a bill set out in McDaniel v. McElvy, 91 Fla. 770, 108 

So. 820, 51 A. L. R. 731. A bill of complaint under the 1925 statute (C. G. L. 

5010 et seq.) must be sworn to. Chapter XXX, Section 333, supra. See Form

No. 7, Appendix B, for form of affidavit. A bill to quiet title under the statutes in existence prior to 1925, and which are still in effect, is contained in Hannay v. Sanchez, 68 Fla. 167, 66 So. 997.

This cause coming on to be heard this day upon the sworn bill of complaint of the plaintiff herein on file, upon the motion of the plaintiff for the appointment of a receiver in accordance with and pursuant to the prayers contained in said bill of complaint, and it appearing that due notice of this hearing has been given to all parties hereto, and the court having heard argument of counsel for the respective parties, and being advised in the premises, it is, upon consideration, ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that Benjamin Brown be and he hereby is appointed receiver of the property and premises described in the plaintiff's bill of complaint herein on file, which said property and premises is situated in the City of Jacksonville, in Duval County, Florida, and is more particularly described as Lot six (6), Block three (3), Avondale, according to plat thereof recorded in Plat Book 17, page 12, of the current public records of Duval County, Florida; and it is further 

ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that the said receiver is hereby authorized, directed, and empowered to enter upon, receive, recover, and take complete, entire, and exclusive possession of said property and premises, to collect the rents, issues, and profits thereof, and to rent and let the same upon a month to month basis; and it is further

FORMS 

911 ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that the receiver shall preserve, maintain, and defend such possession and said property and estate, and the defendants and all persons claiming under them are hereby directed to deliver to said receiver the said property and premises, and to refrain from molesting or interfering with said receiver in the performance of the powers and duties hereby invested in him; and it is further 

ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that the said receiver hereby appointed shall have and is hereby given all of the usual, necessary, and incidental powers of receivers for the purpose of managing and maintaining said property and premises, including the power to make such repairs to the said property as in his judgment are necessary to obtain or retain tenants for the same, and the said receiver shall be at liberty to apply to this court at any time during the pendency of this cause for further directions in the premises; and it is further 

ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that, before the said receiver shall enter upon the performance of his duties as herein prescribed, and before he shall take possession of said property and premises, and as a condition precedent to the taking effect of his appointment as herein made, he shall make and file herein his bond in the sum of five hundred dollars ($500.00), with good and sufficient sureties, to be approved by the clerk of this court, conditioned upon the faithful performance of his duties as such receiver. 

DONE AND ORDERED at Jacksonville, in Duval County, Florida, this 3rd day of November, 1932. Judge

Form No. 19 BILL FOR RESCISSION OF CONVEYANCE ON GROUND OF DURESS 

In the Circuit Court in and for Gulf County, Florida. In Chancery. 

John Doe and 

Mary Doe, his wife, Plaintiffs

VS. 

Bill of Complaint 

Samuel Smith,

Defendant 

John Doe and Mary Doe, his wife, both of whom are residents of the City of Seminole, in Gulf County, Florida, bring this bill of complaint against Samuel Smith, a resident of the City of Seminole, in 

Gulf County, Florida, and allege: 

1. The plaintiff John Doe is and has been for twenty years prior to the filing of this bill of complaint the husband of the plaintiff Mary Doe. 

2. On and prior to May 8, 1910, the plaintiff Mary Doe was the owner in fee simple of that lot or parcel of land lying and being in the City of Seminole, in Gulf County, Florida, more particularly described as Lot ten (10), Block twelve (12), Pine Grove subdivision, according to plat recorded in Plat Book 20, page 35, of the public records of said county. On said May 8, 1910, the plaintiffs John and Mary Doe were occupying said property with their four children as a homestead. 

3. For many years prior to May 8, 1905, the plaintiff John Doe was a Deputy Clerk of the Circuit Court in and for Gulf County, Florida, having been appointed to said position by the defendant Samuel Smith, who is the Clerk of said Circuit Court. In the course of his duties as deputy clerk, it was the duty of the plaintiff John Doe to handle vouchers drawn upon the public funds of said Gulf County, and, just prior to May 8, 1910, the defendant Samuel Smith arrived at the conclusion that certain moneys belonging to said county had been embezzled, or made away with, or wrongfully obtained by some person in the office of the said Samuel Smith, Clerk of the said Circuit Court, and the defendant accused the plaintiff John Doe of being the person who had committed the wrong.

4. The plaintiff John Doe was naturally much disturbed by the making of said charge, and by the stigma that would be cast upon himself and his family if a criminal prosecution should be instituted against him upon the suspicion that he was the person guilty of the embezzlement or diversion aforesaid, and the said plaintiff was desirous of avoiding the said prosecution. The defendant Samuel Smith was desirous of raising money with which to pay the amount of the deficit in the said funds, and the said defendant stated to the plaintiff, John Doe, that he and the State Auditor had been schoolmates and promised and contracted with said John Doe that, if he would cause his wife, the plaintiff Mary Doe, to deed to him the real estate above mentioned, that he, the said defendant, would so arrange matters that no criminal prosecution would be instituted against the said plaintiff 

John Doe. 

5. Relying upon the said promise of the defendant, and solely in consideration thereof, the plaintiff John Doe induced and caused his wife, the plaintiff Mary Doe, to make a conveyance of the said property to the defendant, and the said plaintiff, Mary Doe, on May 8, 1910, in pursuance of said agreement between the defendant and her husband, executed and delivered to the defendant a deed to the said property. A copy of said deed is hereto attached, marked Exhibit "A," and made a part of this bill of complaint. Immediately upon the execution and delivery of said deed to the defendant, he filed the same for record and the said deed was, on May 8, 1910, recorded in Deed Book 25, page 50, of the public records of Gulf County, Florida. 

6. After the defendant had received and recorded the said deed, and in violation of his said contract and promise, he did not arrange that there should be no criminal prosecution against the plaintiff John Doe for the said alleged crime. On the contrary, the said defendant himself instituted a prosecution before R. J. Landum, a justice of the peace of said Gulf County, for the alleged crime, and caused the plaintiff John Doe to be arrested and brought before the said justice of the peace and to be required to furnish bond for his appearance for trial upon said charge before the Criminal Court of Record of said Gulf County. 

7. The real property hereinabove described was the homestead of the plaintiff John Doe and his said wife and family, and was not subject to execution against the plaintiff John Doe. And since the sole

FORMS 

915 consideration upon which the said conveyance of the property was made was the consideration aforesaid, and since that consideration has failed, the plaintiffs are entitled to have the said conveyance cancelled and annulled and to have a reconveyance of the said property by the defendant. 

8. The plaintiff Mary Doe only became aware of the charges made by the defendant, that her husband had embezzled the funds of said county, on the day before the making of the conveyance aforesaid, by the statement of her husband that the charge had been made. Upon the same day, the defendant came to the home of the plaintiffs and remained for a very long time, persuading the plaintiffs to make the said conveyance and promising, as aforesaid, that if it was made he would see that no prosecution was brought against the plaintiff John Doe. The plaintiff Mary Doe was very unwilling to make the said conveyance because the effect of transferring the said property would be to leave her and her children, of which she has and then had four, without a home and penniless, but she has been very sick with a nervous disease for many years, and her nerves were so affected and her mind so weakened by the shock of the communication to her and by the threatened exposure of her husband and his consequent imprisonment in the penitentiary, that she yielded and consented to execute the said deed, and did execute it. The time elapsing between her first knowledge of the charge against her said husband and the execution of the said papers was only the time between the late morning of a Sunday and the early morning of the next day. During this time, the defendant had two interviews with the plaintiff Mary Doe and prevailed upon her to execute the said deed, and finally, when she did so, she was so weak and unstrung that she was compelled to get up from a sick bed to execute the deed and, but for her said nervous and shocked condition and the influence of the defendant and his promise as aforesaid, she would not have executed it. The execution of said deed, under the circumstances aforesaid, was under duress, is not binding upon the plaintiff Mary Doe, and should be set aside by a court of equity. 

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff prays that the said deed to the defendant be cancelled and annulled and that the defendant be decreed to re-convey the said property to the plaintiff Mary Doe. Solicitor for Plaintiffs

Note. The foregoing bill of complaint is copied from a bill set out and held sufficient in Burton v. McMillan, 52 Fla. 469, 42 So. 849, 120 Am. St. Rep. 220, 8 L. R., A. (N. S.) 991, 11 Ann. Cas. 380. A bill to rescind a conveyance for a unilateral mistake of fact is contained in Crosby v. Andrews, 61 Fla. 554, 55

So. 57, Ann. Cas. 1913A, 420. A bill for rescission based upon a mutual mistake is set out in Capital City Bank v. Hilson, 64 Fla. 206, 60 So. 189, Ann.

Cas. 1914B, 1211. The principal allegations of a bill for rescission based upon undue influence are quoted in Adams v. Stringfellow, 91 Fla. 305, 107 So. 633.

The principal allegations of a bill to rescind because of an innocent misrepresentation of fact are stated in Langley v. Irons Land Co., 94 Fla. 1010, 114 

So. 769.

Form No. 20 BILL FOR SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE OF CONTRACT TO SELL LAND 

In the Circuit Court in and for Polk County, Florida. In Chancery. 

VS. 

>Bill of Complaint 

William Smith and 

Mary Smith, his wife,

Defendants 

John Doe, a resident of Boston, Massachusetts, brings this bill of complaint against William Smith and Mary Smith, both of whom are residents of Winter Haven, in Polk County, Florida, and alleges: 

1. On the 21st day of August, 1935, plaintiff and the defendants made and entered into a certain contract in writing, duly executed and acknowledged, wherein and whereby the defendants did agree and obligate themselves to sell and convey to the plaintiff the following described real estate, to wit, Lot six (6), Block seven (7), of Lake

Heights Addition to Winter Haven, together with the buildings thereon, being two apartment houses, situated and being in Polk County, Florida. In and by said contract, the plaintiff did agree and obligate himself to purchase the said property for and at the price of twenty-three thousand dollars ($23,000.00), one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) the receipt of which was then and thereby acknowledged, seven thousand dollars ($7,000.00) on the delivery of an abstract brought down to date, showing the property free and clear of all encumbrances and with a marketable title, and the balance to be evidenced by three notes in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00)

FORMS 

917 each, to become due and payable one, two, and three years after date with 6% interest, and the payment of which was to be secured by a mortgage upon the said property. Said contract was recorded on September 23, 1935, in Deed Book 17, page 92, of the public records of Polk County, Florida, and a copy thereof is hereto attached, marked Exhibit "A," and made a part of this bill of complaint. 

2. It is further provided by said contract that, in the event the purchaser defaulted in the payment of the sum of seven thousand dollars ($7,000.00) due thereunder, then the sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) was to be retained by the vendor as legal damages, and that the agreement was to be closed within thirty days from its date, or as soon thereafter as an abstract of title could be brought down to date, allowing fifteen days for the attorney for the purchaser to approve the said abstract. 

3. After securing the said contract and making the payment of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) therein provided for, plaintiff went to his home in Boston for the purpose of making necessary arrangements for returning to Florida and making his home in Winter Haven upon the property hereinabove described. On September 22, 1935, plaintiff left 

Boston for Florida with the intention of closing the said purchase, as he believed he had a right to do. Plaintiff is a person of but little experience in business transactions and the meaning of contracts, but he understood the meaning of said contract to be that the said transaction was to be closed within thirty days from the delivery of the abstract, which was in fact delivered on September 8, 1935. Plaintiff is now advised and informed that, under the terms of said contract, he was required to pay to the defendants the sum of seven thousand dollars ($7,000.00) upon the delivery of the abstract, but plaintiff did not so understand the contract at the time it was made. Upon arriving in Winter Haven, plaintiff sought out the defendants with a view of completing the said purchase, accepting a deed of conveyance, and making payment of the proper sums and complying with his contract as he understood the same, but the plaintiff was informed by the said defendants that he had lost his rights under said contract by failing to pay the said sum of seven thousand dollars ($7,000.00) upon the delivery of the abstract and that the thirty days in which the transaction was to have been closed had expired. The defendants thereupon refused to carry out the sale and execute the deed of conveyance to the plaintiff, claiming that they were released from their contract and

were entitled to retain the one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) as damages, notwithstanding the fact that the plaintiff advised them that he desired to complete said purchase and was ready, able, and willing to comply with the terms of the contract and to make the payments thereby required. 

4. Plaintiff has long been a resident of Boston, Massachusetts, and was desirous of changing his domicile therefrom to the State of Florida and, before making up his mind as to the place best suited to him in which he might make a home in Florida, he inspected various pieces of property, none of which suited him except the property hereinabove described. After viewing said property he was convinced that it would fill his requirements and tastes better than any other property in the community, and plaintiff decided to buy the said property and make it his home and domicile. Plaintiff knows of no other property which he could buy at a price in keeping with his means and ability and which would as well meet his requirements for a home and domicile. No amount of damages would compensate the plaintiff for the loss of the home he had planned to establish upon this particular piece of property. 

5. The contract between plaintiff and defendants has no provision making time of the essence thereof, and the defendants have no right to declare the said contract forfeited by reason of the failure of the plaintiff to comply strictly therewith and without giving the plaintiff sufficient notice of their intention to terminate said contract, which notice has not been given. 

6. According to the terms of the said contract, the defendants are only entitled to retain the said sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) as damages for the failure of the plaintiff to comply with the terms of the contract. But, should this court deem it proper and according to the rules of equity for plaintiff to bear that loss and pay to the defendants the said sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) as damages, the plaintiff is now and will be ready, able and willing, upon the court's decision in the matter, to pay to the defendants an additional sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) in order to secure a conveyance of the said property by the defendants.

WHEREFORE, the plaintiff prays that this court, at the final hearing hereof, determine whether or not the plaintiff shall pay to the defendants the additional sum of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) as 1

FORMS 

919 damages, and that the defendants, William Smith and Mary Smith, his wife, be decreed to make, execute, and deliver to the plaintiff their warranty deed conveying a clear and marketable title to the said property in accordance with the terms of their said contract. 

Solicitor for Plaintiff Note. A bill of complaint similar in all material respects to the foregoing form was held sufficient in Dugan v. Powell, 91 Fla. 1034, 109 So. 202. Another bill for specific performance which was held sufficient is set out in Beekman v. Sonntag Inv. Co., 67 Fla. 293, 64 So. 948.

Order of Reference 

Richard Roe and 

William Smith,

Defendants This cause coming on to be heard this day upon the plaintiff's motion for the appointment of a special master herein, and it appearing from the court files herein that this cause is now at issue upon the answer of the defendant Richard Roe, and that a decree pro confesso has been duly and regularly entered against the defendant William Smith, and this cause being now ready for reference, it is, upon consideration, ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that George Green,
